subject: Request: carve-out to liability cap for trade-secret loss / MSA redline

Subject: MSA redline – confidentiality / trade secret carve-out request

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we’re excited about using Redwood for inference across our analytics stacks. Our legal team took a first pass at the MSA and attached a redline. Two asks surfaced from procurement and legal: 1) they want an explicit carve-out to the liability cap for losses resulting from unauthorized exfiltration of StellarNow trade secrets, and 2) a narrow right to forensic costs and injunctive relief.

Can your legal team propose language we can agree on? I attached the redline (StellarNow_MSA_redline_20260906.pdf) and a short evidence-preservation checklist procurement wants included in the SOW.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement committee meets Friday.

Best,
Jordan Phelps
VP, Legal Ops
StellarNow

—Marcus

Subject: RE: MSA redline – confidentiality / trade secret carve-out request

Quick notes after reading Jordan’s redline and the checklist:
- StellarNow proposes an unlimited-exception for "trade secrets"; we need a narrower definition (e.g., "Confidential Information that is both: (i) clearly marked and identified as trade secrets; and (ii) demonstrably subject to reasonable access controls by the Customer and documented in writing prior to the incident").
- Tie the carve-out to a breach that results from Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct. We should not accept a carve-out for any third-party breach where StellarNow failed to follow the evidence-preservation checklist.
- Forensic cost bucket: propose a capped amount (e.g., up to $250,000) to cover immediate investigative expenses; anything beyond that could be subject to indemnity rules and dependent on findings.
- Injunctive relief: preserve equitable remedies, but specify that injunctive relief does not enlarge damages beyond the cap except to the extent required by law.

I’ll draft the target language below for Marcus to approve before we send.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redline – confidentiality / trade secret carve-out request

Adding operational points:
- We need the right to perform an independent analysis of the incident with limited scope — Redwood’s security team will need to collect logs and may need to coordinate with StellarNow’s security contacts. Require written consent for any destructive testing.
- Require the customer to initiate preservation steps within 48 hours of notice (we can accept 72 hours in exceptional circumstances), otherwise carve-out is voidable.
- Clarify the burden of proof: StellarNow must demonstrate by a preponderance of evidence that the loss was caused by Redwood’s breach, and production of forensic report within a reasonable timeframe (30 days) is required to trigger any expanded recovery.

Rishi
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Phelps <jordan.phelps@stellarnow.com>, Amir Khan <amir.khan@stellarnow.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, contracts@stellarnow.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed wording – limited trade-secret carve-out (MSA §9)

Jordan / Amir — thanks for the quick turnaround. Below is the language we can accept as a balanced compromise; we’ve tried to keep it narrow and operational:

"Notwithstanding Section 9 (Limitation of Liability), neither party's liability for direct damages shall be capped with respect to claims arising from: (i) willful misconduct or gross negligence resulting in the unauthorized access, acquisition or exfiltration of the other party's Trade Secrets, as defined below, and (ii) reasonable, documented third-party forensic and preservation costs incurred within thirty (30) days following discovery of the incident, up to an aggregate cap of Two Hundred Fifty Thousand US Dollars (USD 250,000).

For purposes of this Section, 'Trade Secrets' means Confidential Information that (a) the disclosing party designates in writing as a trade secret prior to disclosure, (b) is subject to documented reasonable access controls, and (c) the disclosing party reasonably treated as confidential. Any claim under this carve-out requires: (1) written notice to the other party within ten (10) days of discovery; (2) initiation by Customer of the evidence-preservation steps set forth in the mutually agreed preservation checklist within forty-eight (48) hours of discovery (or within seventy-two (72) hours in documented exceptional circumstances); and (3) delivery of a forensic report demonstrating by a preponderance of evidence that Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence caused the exfiltration.

Injunctive and other equitable relief shall remain available without regard to the liability cap but shall not be used to expand recoverable damages beyond the caps set forth herein except as compelled by applicable law."

If that reads OK to you, we can incorporate this into the MSA and return a clean PDF. If StellarNow prefers a higher forensic-cost cap, indicate the number and we’ll see whether commercial can take it (Marcus).

—Marcus

We can agree to the written designation requirement for trade secrets if StellarNow can designate up to 10 items retroactively within 30 days of execution (we’ll provide a matrix).

If you can accept those, procurement is prepared to move to signature this week.

Best,
Jordan
